source: credential masking on GET/PUT /mockserver/configuration. isolated because it PUTs configuration properties (dataPlaneAuthenticationRequired, dataPlaneBearerAuthenticationToken, …) that reset does not clear and that would otherwise leak into every scenario run after this one on the shared replay server.

steps.note: defaults: whole-value and write-only-omitted credentials absent; embedded ones present empty
set the three whole-value credentials
clearing a whole-value credential with an empty string makes it absent again
a value merely CONTAINING the mask, alongside an edited neighbour: refused, not half-applied
the mask-carrying llmApiKey is refused; proxyAuthenticationRealm still applies and the PUT is not rejected
clusterFanInPeerAuthToken: settable, never disclosed either way (the named regression)
llmBackendsConfig: set two backends, one with a credential-named field
renaming the masked backend leaves it with no held counterpart: the whole document is refused, unchanged
an edit to the non-secret ollama baseUrl applies; the masked openai apiKey is restored from the held value
prometheusRemoteWriteHeaders: a credential header alongside an ordinary one
editing the ordinary header and adding a new one applies; the masked Authorization is restored
two headers differing only in case both get a credential-shaped name
a third casing cannot be resolved unambiguously against either held header: refused, unchanged
a header value containing a comma cannot be represented by k=v,k2=v2 (no escape): masked whole, tail absorbed
echoing that masked whole-comma value straight back is the unedited round trip: unchanged
privateKeyPath is readable despite its credential-shaped name (a file path, not a secret)
a mask-carrying value pasted onto it (as if copied from a diagnostic surface) is refused, unchanged
dataPlaneBearerAuthenticationToken end to end: an expectation to probe against

require data-plane bearer auth and set the token: absent from GET (write-only), but must actually take effect — before the fix this silently no-op'd, because the generic PUT path only recognised properties already present in the (masked) GET output
wrong bearer: 401
correct bearer: reaches the expectation
capture the current (masked, token-omitting) configuration to echo straight back
GET-then-PUT round trip: the whole captured body, which carries no dataPlaneBearerAuthenticationToken field at all
the token must survive the round trip: still reaches the expectation
and the wrong bearer is still rejected — auth is still enforced
